claim: truncate_utf8_by_bytes decides whether the input fits by Str.length(s), a character count, not its byte length, so any input with characters <= max_bytes < bytes is returned whole and over the cap: "éé" (4 bytes) with max_bytes 2 comes back as all 4 bytes.
witness: s = "éé" (UTF-8 c3 a9 c3 a9), max_bytes = 2 -> result c3 a9 c3 a9 (4 bytes)
notes: Cause: store.ail:22 `let n = Str.length(s);` (rune count); the byte value `b` is built on line 21 but only used for the slice. Seen by reading line 22, then confirmed by execution on the real function (export shim, one word changed): 46,422 of 88,292 cases with n >= 0 (chars <= 6), 273/9,254 (bytes <= 3), 10,916/19,112 (random, 20,000), 300/498 (random, up to 2,000 chars), 5/11 (CJK). The result can be up to 4x max_bytes (all 4-byte chars). Negative control: the same shim with `length(b)` in place of `Str.length(s)` gives 0 of 88,292. REACHABLE: the only caller, store_stdout_and_elide (compose.ail:723), calls it exactly when the byte length > max_stdout_bytes, and every violation shows through it unchanged (ailcaller:P6.1 has the same counts). At compose's default cap of 4000, 1,400 x U+6F22 (4,200 bytes) is returned whole plus the notice, with truncated:true and nothing elided: `bash /home/motoko/trial-043/s/t043-t6-a1/out/repro/repro.sh A1-T6-1-caller` exits 1.

claim: (Known, K2) truncate_utf8_by_bytes slices at a raw byte offset and the result can end inside a character, so valid UTF-8 comes back invalid: "éa" with max_bytes 1 returns the lone lead byte c3.
witness: s = "éa" (UTF-8 c3 a9 61), max_bytes = 1 -> result c3 (1 byte, invalid UTF-8)
notes: Registered as known-violated (K2); RESEARCH §7 notes it by reading. Confirmed by execution: 16,348/93,753 (chars <= 6), 4,071/20,000 (random), 121/500 (long random), 3/11 (CJK). std/bytes.toString does no repair, so the partial character travels on and P6.2 still holds (0 violations on every generator, including non-UTF-8 inputs). The rune gate of A1-T6-1 hides part of K2 by returning whole strings: with the gate changed to bytes, P6.3 fails 46,422/93,753. So fixing A1-T6-1 alone makes this more frequent. Reachable through store_stdout_and_elide with the same counts (ailcaller:P6.3). A boundary back-off control (T6_MUTANT=fixed) gives 0 violations, and this repro then exits 0.

claim: The TypeScript twin truncateUtf8ByBytes in compose-claimcheck.ts decodes the cut bytes with Buffer.toString("utf8"), which turns a split character into U+FFFD, so the text can be longer than maxBytes and is not a byte prefix of the input: "é" with maxBytes 1 returns "\uFFFD" (3 bytes).
witness: s = "é" (UTF-8 c3 a9), maxBytes = 1 -> text ef bf bd (3 bytes), truncated true
notes: X-4 = P6.1 and P6.2a together, applied to this twin (compose-claimcheck.ts:104-109). Called through the real exported runClaimCheck (env-server.ts:1810) with a stub callStream that captures the informalizer prompt, and also by source extraction. P6.1 fails 38,685/88,292 and the byte-prefix property fails 46,422/93,753 (chars <= 6). The overshoot is at most 2 bytes. P6.3 holds (0), which is the reverse of the AILANG target's trade-off. REACHABLE: runClaimCheck passes Math.max(1, stdoutMaxBytes), 4,000 by default, so any certificate stdout over the cap that is cut mid-character reaches the informalizer prompt with U+FFFD. Every AILANG/TS disagreement (62,770 on chars <= 6) is explained by A1-T6-1 or this defect (TWINX 0 unexplained). A fixed twin (back off to a character boundary) gives 0 violations, and this repro's check exits 0 on it.

claim: compose-claimcheck.ts truncateUtf8ByBytes counts omittedBytes as input bytes minus the bytes of the U+FFFD-expanded text, so the "[truncated: N bytes omitted]" note under-reports: "é" with maxBytes 1 says truncated with 0 bytes omitted.
witness: s = "é" (UTF-8 c3 a9), maxBytes = 1 -> truncated true, omittedBytes 0 (expected 2); "héllo", 2 -> 2 (expected 5)
notes: X-2: when truncated, omittedBytes should equal |in| minus the longest common byte prefix of the input and the text. Fails on every mid-character cut: 46,422/82,831 truncated cases (chars <= 6), 10,571/18,664 (random). Math.max(0, ...) clamps the negative difference to 0. Seen through the real exported runClaimCheck: the informalizer prompt ends "[truncated: 0 bytes omitted]". Same root cause as A1-T6-3 but a separate wrong output (a count, not the text). The fixed-twin control gives 0.
